name: IT-RAT
description: The open-source agent-governance stack, and the guides that explain it.

pages.title: IT-RAT, the agent-governance stack
pages.description: Open-source runtime governance for AI agents: budgets, policy, memory, identity, cryptography, quality and pre-production drills. Apache-2.0, self-hosted.

pages.title: Genaryx, the console over the stack
pages.description: Genaryx: one browser control room over the whole agent stack, on your own box. Passkey-signed kills, WireGuard-only reach and signed evidence packs.

pages.title: Guides index
pages.description: Ten guides: six on the field of AI agent governance, and four on running this stack in practice, from a first alert to what the numbers prove.

pages.title: AI agent governance
pages.description: What AI agent governance means in practice: budgets, policy, identity, provenance, quality and drills applied while an agent runs, not after.

pages.title: FinOps for AI
pages.description: FinOps applied to LLM and agent spend: the unit of work, per-run budgets, reserve-then-settle, FOCUS showback and cost per resolved case.

pages.title: AI agent security
pages.description: The failure modes an autonomous agent introduces, the runtime guardrail that answers each one, and how to rehearse them in CI. Defensive practice.

pages.title: MCP security
pages.description: What changes when tools arrive over the Model Context Protocol: descriptions the model reads, servers nobody sanctioned, tools that change later.

pages.title: Agent identity and authentication
pages.description: Static keys are not identity. What an AI agent needs to be nameable, attributable, attestable and revocable, and when to demand a signature.

pages.title: Glossary of agent-governance terms
pages.description: Plain definitions for this field: agent passport, attestation, delegation chain, blast radius, per-run budget, rug pull, CBOM, FOCUS, drift.

pages.title: AI observability vs governance
pages.description: LLM observability explains what an agent did; governance decides what it may do next. Where each fails, and how they meet on one run id.

pages.title: One incident, end to end
pages.description: A single runaway agent followed through spend, policy, identity, memory, mail and evidence: what each plane sees, what it emits, and who is told.

pages.title: What runs where and what it costs
pages.description: One machine, a five-node cluster, or three clouds: the measured shapes of this stack, what each burns per hour, and the storage line that changes by 108x.

pages.title: From zero to your first alert
pages.description: One command, one address, one mail: the shortest honest path from nothing to a governed agent that writes to you when it crosses a line.

pages.title: What is proven and what is not
pages.description: How to read a validation claim: what was measured on this stack, what the measurement does not cover, and the conclusions we published and had to withdraw.

pages.title: TokenFuse, the money plane
pages.description: A drop-in gateway that gives every agent run a budget and answers 402 the moment it is crossed. Raft-replicated, validated on Hetzner, AWS and GCP.

pages.title: Wardryx, the policy plane
pages.description: The policy plane your agents ask before acting: allow, deny or hold for a human, with signed approval tokens and a hard ceiling that outranks approvals.

pages.title: Idryx, the access plane
pages.description: One identity graph for humans, keys, service accounts and AI agents: delegation chains, blast radius, 22 deterministic detectors and a CycloneDX Agent-BOM.

pages.title: Engram, the knowledge plane
pages.description: Embeddable agent memory in one SQLite file: bitemporal facts, hybrid BM25 and vector recall, why() provenance and GDPR forget. No server, no API key to start.

pages.title: Qryx, the crypto plane
pages.description: Inventory every key, certificate and algorithm you actually run, grade the post-quantum risk against the NCSC 2028, 2031 and 2035 dates, sign the evidence.

pages.title: Verdryx, the quality plane
pages.description: Cost per correctly resolved case, not cost per token: five graders, statistical drift detection and a metered LLM judge, scored on your own outcome tags.

pages.title: Mockryx, the pre-production plane
pages.description: Fire drills for your guardrails: YAML scenarios fired at a real gateway, asserting the 402, the 403 and the downstream reaction. Zero real spend, CI-native.

pages.title: Heraldyx, the alerts plane
pages.description: The part of the agent stack that writes to you: it reads the shared event log, decides what is worth a human tonight, and mails it with one link.

pages.title: Scopyx, the egress plane
pages.description: Your agents already reach the web and nothing governs it. Scopyx decides every destination before anything leaves, and keeps origins rather than URLs.

pages.title: Trailryx, the record
pages.description: A record of what your AI agents did that nobody can quietly change or shorten, where every answer carries a proof that it is complete.

pages.title: Platform, the shared contract
pages.description: One agent:// passport, one event envelope, one Go binding and a Terraform provider: the shared contract under all seven services of the stack. Apache-2.0.
